messages:
Lena (People Ops): Quick heads-up: new minimal change to PTO policy going live today — a 'Bereavement Flex' option. If you need time for bereavement or urgent caregiving you can now request up to 5 days immediate paid leave via the portal; managers should expect an auto-acknowledgement and People Ops will follow-up for documentation as needed. https://redwood.company/hr/bereavement :pray:
Omar (Eng): Appreciate this. Is it separate from emergency leave?
Lena (People Ops): Yes — Bereavement Flex is for short immediate needs and is intended to be low-friction. Emergency leave covers relocation, extended care, or events needing >5 days and uses the existing exception workflow.
Priya (Sales): Any records on payroll/tax? Will finance see these as standard PTO?
George (Finance): They'll appear as a distinct line "Bereavement Flex" on payroll. Tax treatment depends on country — we'll flag cases requiring gross-up. Reach out if you need country-specific guidance.
Omar (Eng): Can managers retro-approve if someone needed the time but forgot to file?
Lena (People Ops): Managers can retro-approve up to 7 days. Beyond that, People Ops handles ad-hoc approvals. We want to keep it simple for folks under stress.
HR Bot: Reminder: use the Bereavement Flex form for immediate requests. Missing info will delay review.
Priya (Sales): Will contractors be eligible?
Lena (People Ops): Short answer: no for standard contractors. Contractors on payroll may be considered case-by-case. Check with your recruiter or People Ops rep.
George (Finance): Ops note: we'll include a short report in monthly payroll exports so managers can reconcile balances.
Lena (People Ops): Thanks everyone. We'll monitor usage for 60 days and share metrics. If any edge cases pop up DM me or post in #people-ops. :heart:
